lines.trans: Whose phone call are you waiting for?
Wait for what? I am not waiting for anyone.
How should I know where he is! He turned his phone off and can wander wherever he likes.
So you did try calling him, seeing how you know his phone is off.
I just tried calling him once.
Listen to me without getting offended.
You need to leave a small gap open.
But my sister cannot wait at all. There is zero breathing room.
You reply right away every time, so the other person never gets a moment to wonder about you.
When there is no reply, the other person starts wondering why you have not answered.
Oh, forget it! You are telling me to play hard to get.
I am just saying to leave time for thought in a relationship between two people.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가
indefinite pronoun

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

meanings.note: Sino-Korean word for telephone.

examples.trans: A phone call came.
I will hang up the phone.
I want to wait right now.
How about trying to wait together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2
I want to turned off and right now.
How about trying to turned off and together tomorrow?

놓다.gloss: to put, to place, to leave

meanings.en: to put, to place, to leave
meanings.note: Often used as an auxiliary verb to indicate leaving something in a certain state.

examples.trans: Please place it on the desk.
I left the door open.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?

meanings.en: to go around, to attend, to commute
meanings.note: Indicates regular movement or carrying something around constantly.

examples.trans: I commute to the company.
I carry a bag around with me.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

meanings.note: The person called is marked with 에게 or 한테 (e.g., 친구한테 전화하다).

examples.trans: Please call me when you arrive.
I'll call right now.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
I want to turned off right now.
How about trying to turned off together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: commonly paired with 좋다 ('good') or 나쁘다 ('bad')

examples.trans: The weather is clear, so I'm in a good mood.

examples.text: 칭찬을 들으니 기분이 날아갈 것 같아요.
examples.trans: Hearing the compliment makes me feel on cloud nine.
Let's feel offended together today.
I worked hard to feel offended yesterday too.

meanings.note: verb listen

examples.trans: Listen well.
Listen to a song.

meanings.en: lightly, gently, just a tiny bit
meanings.note: Mimetic adverb often used to minimize damage or effort.

examples.trans: The door opened slightly.
The car got a tiny nick.
Did you hear about this gap, room?
I was busy today because of gap, room.
I want to opens right now.
How about trying to opens together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.en: older sister; older female friend or senior
meanings.note: Used by a younger male speaker.

examples.trans: I have one older sister.
Nuna, do you have time today?

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
I understand well (immediately every time).
Today is a (immediately every time) busy day.

meanings.note: 답이 없다 ('there is no answer') is a common idiom meaning a situation is hopeless.

examples.trans: There's really no answer to this problem.
I found the answer to the question.

meanings.note: Used for giving things to someone of equal or lower status.

examples.trans: I gave a gift.
Please give me some water.
Did you hear about this the other person?
I was busy today because of the other person.

meanings.en: to be curious; to wonder about
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective in Korean; the thing wondered about takes -이/가.

examples.trans: I'm really curious about the result.
If you have anything you're curious about, please ask.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: noun thought

examples.trans: Good idea.
Come to mind.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!
Let's play push and pull together today.
I worked hard to play push and pull yesterday too.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.
Did you hear about this relationship?
I was busy today because of relationship.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean term for human or logical relations.

examples.trans: human relations
What is the relationship between those two?
Let's I think together today.
I worked hard to I think yesterday too.

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

meanings.note: casual greeting or farewell

examples.trans: Hi! Have you been well?
See you tomorrow, bye!
